question: During vacuum extraction, the cup must be applied at the 'flexion point'. Where is this point located?

answers.text: Over the anterior fontanelle to maximise traction force

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Placement over the anterior fontanelle produces deflexion and asynclitism, increasing the effective diameter of the presenting head and the risk of failure and scalp trauma.

answers.text: 3 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle, in the midline sagittal suture

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The flexion point is 3 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle along the sagittal suture. Cup placement here promotes flexion and synclitism, presenting the smallest fetal head diameter to the pelvis.

Placement directly over the posterior fontanelle is too posterior; correct placement is 3 cm anterior to it in the midline. Placement at the posterior fontanelle itself promotes excessive flexion and does not allow synclitism correction.

answers.text: At the most accessible point on the fetal head depending on the station

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The flexion point is anatomically fixed regardless of station. Applying the cup at the most accessible point without regard to the flexion point leads to malpositioned traction and increased failure rates.

overallFeedback.feedback: The flexion point for ventouse cup placement is 3 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle in the midline — this position promotes flexion and synclitism, presenting the smallest head diameter.
Correct. Applying the cup at the flexion point (3 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle, midline) is the single most important technical principle of vacuum extraction.
